text:
sam: Hi team — Nimbus Insurance is asking for a 3-week POC. They need streaming + function/tool-calling for structured claims extraction, SOC2 evidence, and an upfront pricing estimate for a short reserved capacity trial. Can someone help with an engineer-facing runbook + quick pricing note?

jenna: Which SDKs are they using? Node + Python? Any JVM components?

sam: Mostly Node for the frontend orchestration, Python for backend workers. They also have a small Go adapter.

miguel: I can put together an example stream + functioncall that returns structured JSON for claims. Quick sample (Node):
```js
const r = await client.stream({
  model: 'redwood-large-v2',
  stream: true,
  tools: [{name: 'extract_claim', spec: {...}}],
  input: 'Customer email: \"I slipped on wet floor...\"',
  structured_output: true
});
r.on('function_call', (call) => {
  // call tool, then r.resume({tool_result})
});
```
This shows function/tool calling and structured_output. Use small token windows for each tool call and prefer SSE if they can't keep websockets.

devon: Engineering note: for claims that exceed 4k tokens use prefix KV caching to avoid re-tokenizing the whole policy doc. For POC set batch_size=1, max_concurrency=4, and use the 8-bit quantized variant if latency needs to be lower. Also set the fallback policy to 'smaller-model' for graceful degradation.

priya: Security checklist for the SOC2/legal team: we need answers for data residency, retention, KMS usage, and subprocessor list. Are they planning to send PII into the hosted API? If yes we should propose Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem. I can pre-fill the questionnaire if someone drops the customer's security contact. Also: redact PII at ingestion or use client-side encryption for tokens.

elaine: Pricing for a 3-week reserved POC: typical approach is a short reserved commitment covering baseline throughput + burst. For a small POC (1-2 qps sustained), propose a $6k reserved bucket + usage overage at list rates. If legal needs a formal discount we can do a 20% POC discount and a one-time credit for testing. This is flexible but needs approval from deal desk for enterprise accounts.

sam: Good — can you write that in a short handoff we can send to Nimbus? Also need a yes/no from eng on whether SSE is supported for toolcall live responses (they'll stream parse updates to the UI).

devon: SSE is supported for streaming generative responses. For tool/function calling that triggers external HTTP calls from our runtime, SSE can stream intermediate events but if you need bi-directional low-latency (tool results back into the model in real time) websockets are better. Workaround: emit a function_call event via SSE, have the adapter call the tool, then post the result to the model via the resumable token endpoint.

miguel: Small gotcha — structured_output combined with function calling: make sure the model role of the tool matches the expected schema. If they use strict JSON schema we recommend schema-first asserts on the client and server with simple fallback text for malformed outputs.

priya: For the questionnaire I need: 1) customer security contact 2) example data flows (sample headers/payloads ok) 3) whether logs should be retained for >30 days. If they require audit logs retained beyond our default, we'll need an add-on.

jenna: I'll prepare a simple POC playbook and share a sample Postman collection and minimal code snippets.

devon: Quick runbook snippet (drop-in):
```yaml
POC_RUNBOOK:
  - env: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REGION=us-west-2
  - stream: curl -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large-v2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"input":"...","structured_output":true}'
  - function_call: on 'function_call' event POST to /adapter/extract -> adapter returns JSON -> call /streams/resume with tool_result
  - observability: enable trace_id=X-TRACE and set logs=error+warn for POC
```
This should get their frontend devs streaming partial claim JSON while backend workers call the extraction tool.

elaine: I'll prepare the short pricing note and send as a PDF to Sam by EOD.

sam: Action items: Jenna -> Postman + examples by tomorrow; Miguel -> final Node/Python snippets w/ toolcall by EOD; Devon -> short ops runbook + recommended runtime config; Priya -> prefilled security questionnaire template + list of required customer items; Elaine -> pricing note + draft SOW. Target: draft customer email by 24 hours. :thumbsup:

redwood-bot: Reminder: please tag the thread with #poc-handovers when ready so sales-ops can track the deliverables.

sam: Thanks all — I’ll loop in the Nimbus contact after we have the package.
